question: Should OpenClaw permanently add `write.append` and optional `SandboxFsBridge.appendFile` with a guarantee against stale read-modify-write loss but no whole-call record-atomicity guarantee after partial writes?
rationale: Source review supports the implementation direction, but only maintainers can accept the permanent model-facing and Plugin SDK contract plus its bounded concurrency guarantee.

options.title: Accept bounded native append
options.body: Approve capability-gated EOF append that prevents stale overwrite loss while explicitly disclaiming whole-call record atomicity.

options.title: Require a record-oriented primitive
options.body: Defer the public API until a stronger storage contract can guarantee record-level concurrency semantics.

options.title: Keep write overwrite-only
options.body: Decline the general tool and bridge surface and solve only higher-level memory or state workflows.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded native append
recommendation.body: Approve capability-gated EOF append that prevents stale overwrite loss while explicitly disclaiming whole-call record atomicity.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership of the central write runtime, pinned mutation helper, and OpenShell sandbox architecture.
